title: Jonah Coleman earns bigger role with Broncos in 2026 season
seoTitle: Jonah Coleman Earns Larger Role with Broncos
subtitle: The former Husky prepares to take on more responsibilities in Week 2
excerpt: After a modest debut, former Washington Huskies player Jonah Coleman is ready to take on a larger role in the Denver Broncos' offense.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Jonah Coleman's name reappeared in searches and among football fans' social media feeds after the Denver Broncos took the field in Week 2 of the 2026 season. The former Washington Huskies player, who was selected in the fourth round of the draft, had a debut without huge numbers, but his team's situation quickly changed, creating an opportunity for him to stand out.

Modest debut, but with potential

In his first NFL game against the Kansas City Chiefs, Coleman accumulated just 27 yards on a kickoff return, his only recorded action in a 31-10 loss. However, his experience on the field already showed that he possesses qualities that catch the coaches' attention.

The impact of R.J. Harvey on the team

Broncos starting running back R.J. Harvey suffered a hamstring injury and, according to ESPN, is not expected to return to play. Harvey had been responsible for seven touches in the game against the Chiefs—three rushes and four receptions—and was the one leading most third-down attempts. Harvey's absence opens up a spot for Coleman to take on more responsibilities.

Sean Payton's comments on the young running back

Head coach Sean Payton described Coleman as "smart," "intelligent," and having "good contact balance ability." In an interview with reporter Aric DiLalla, Payton highlighted that Coleman's speed of adaptation may be greater than that of other players who arrived more slowly, thanks to his pass-protection background with the Huskies.

Coaching and development at the professional level

During his two years in Washington, Coleman was praised by Jedd Fisch's staff for his ability to protect the quarterback and catch passes. That reputation has carried over to the NFL level, where the Denver coaching staff values players who can perform as "pass protectors" and "receivers out of the backfield."

Outlook for the game against the Jaguars

With the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars approaching, coach Payton believes Coleman can make a difference in Week 2. He still acknowledges that the youngster has a lot to learn and that his goal is to keep growing and becoming a good teammate.

Conclusion

Although Jonah Coleman's debut was modest, the Denver Broncos' current situation puts him in a prominent position. If he capitalizes on the opportunity, he could become one of the team's key offensive players in the 2026 season.
